title: perf(canary): automated latency/throughput regression detection + rollout guards
author: Aisha Patel
description: Adds end-to-end automated detection for latency and throughput regressions in the performance canary pipeline and implements rollout guards that prevent unsafe traffic shifts when regressions are detected. Motivation: customers have had surprising latency regressions during model rollouts; we need an automated canary that (1) continuously monitors key perf signals, (2) automatically flags statistically significant regressions, and (3) halts or rolls back rollouts using simple, auditable guard rules. This PR contains the detector algorithm, integration with the rollout service, observability hooks, unit and e2e tests, and docs. Design summary: 1) Detector service computes rolling-window latency/throughput distributions and applies sequential hypothesis testing (CUSUM + bootstrap CI) tuned to our workload percentiles; 2) A hysteresis layer prevents flapping by requiring sustained deviation for 3 consecutive windows or a configurable cumulative impact threshold; 3) Rollout guards subscribe to detector alerts and evaluate policy rules (latency_pct_95 > baseline * 1.20 OR throughput_drop > 10%) to stop or throttle traffic. Backwards compatibility: detector publishes events to existing perf-canary topic and exposes metrics tagged by model/version/region so dashboards and alerting reuse current conventions. Testing: unit tests for detector math and rule evaluation, integration tests in tests/perf that simulate injected latency and throughput drops, and manual canary run in perf-canary lab. Checklist: - [x] detector algorithm implemented - [x] guard integration with rollout service - [x] metrics + traces added - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs and runbook updates - [x] changelog/release notes included Commits summary: "Add detector core and windowing logic"; "Integrate detector with rollout service via perf-canary topic"; "Add hysteresis + policy evaluation"; "Add e2e tests and docs"; "Fix flakiness in integration test by increasing sample windows". CI: all checks passed after one retry (lint->fail on first run due to import ordering, fixed). Merge method: squash with descriptive commit message and release note entry.
